newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda bourse to be launched on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Uganda bourse to be launched on Thursday.

text.p: The Kampala Stock Exchange will be launched in the Ugandan capital tomorrow, officials said on Wednesday.

Simon Rutega, coordinator of capital markets at the (central) Bank of Uganda, said five merchant banks would open brokerage subsidiaries for the new market. A sixth had applied to offer brokerage services but had not yet met basic requirements.

Rutega would not say how many companies would be listed at the launch, although government officials have previously said Uganda Grain Milling Co and Uganda Consolidated Properties Ltd would be the first companies traded on the Kampala bourse.

"We are still on target. We finalised analysis of the business proposals and have now shortlisted members," Rutega told Reuters. The launch is scheduled for 9.00 a.m. local (0600 GMT) at the Kampala Sheraton Hotel, itself government-owned.

The companies cleared to open brokerage subsidiaries are Stanbic Bank, Barclays Bank, The Merchant Bank of East Africa, NDC Capital Alliance and Trans Africa Bank, Rutega said. He said the choices were based on these companies' experience.
"The companies have international experience, credibility, capital requirements and confidence of the public; and we are confident that they will have a quality market," Rutega said.
He said Uganda Commercial Bank (UCB), which the government has listed for sale, had also wanted to offer brokerage services but had so far failed to meet some key requirements.
Market analysts saw the UCB application as strange because the government has said it will sell some of its shareholding in the bank through a public flotation on the Kampala bourse.

Minister of State (deputy minister) for privatisation Matthew Rukikaire told reporters last week that the government would inject $70-80 million in bonds into Uganda Commercial Bank in order to make it attractive to any serious buyers.

"As it is, no one can buy Uganda Commercial Bank. It is insolvent. Even if you offered it totally for free, no one would take it, because they would have to seek out the bank's debts," Rukikaire told a news conference.
Brokers will have to pass an examination prepared by the Capital Markets Authority. Rutega said no additional brokerage houses would be licensed in the near future.
"The market is small. You have to limit it first because of professionality. So these (brokers) are more than enough people for the time being," he said.
In a November newsletter, Uganda privatisations team leader Otweyo-Orono listed 15 state companies targeted for flotation.
These included Uganda Commercial Bank, Uganda Airlines, Uganda Posts and Telecommunications, Uganda Consolidated Properties, Uganda Grain Milling Co, Uganda Railways Corp and Dairy Corp.

A recent sale of part of the government's stake in Uganda Grain Milling Co sparked protests because the government ignored the highest bid -- from Kenya's Unga Ltd -- and offered the milling concern to Caleb International, a Ugandan company owned by a brother to Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni.
Minister Rukikaire said that decision was taken to avoid a regional grain milling monopoly by Unga Ltd.
